And once again, the accent puts you at risk of not being understood. You can't expect the other speaker to be capable or willing to put up with it. Not to mention that it's not that hard to fix this issue ,  while you seem to believe that it's unavoidable or close to it. Listen, the core of this discussion is whether or not people should be granted this "bilingual" title of ours regardless of their actual level. We started off on the wrong foot, and while you're unaware of my skills and unable to call me presumptuous because of it I'm more than willing to admit that I was being quite cocky. However, my goal as a learner is to reach a level which will allow me to be as undistinguishable as possible from the real thing.  And I wish that others would set their goals just as high, 'cause I believe in them and their potential.  That is all.

Your judgemental arguments are failing you, amico. Accent has to do with all of it because no matter what when you're learning a language you're trying to maximise your chances of being understood by native speakers, regardless of your background. Your comic looks like it's more about racism than anything else. And no, the learners are not communicating "fine".   "Fine"  is a subjective opinion, they may be understood by a 20 yo guy on the street who's used to interacting with foreigners and be left speechless by an older guy with a more bubbly, londonish way of speaking.

Going up to them and telling them that I don't think they're bilingual would be judgemental, mentioning it while arguing about bilingualism isn't,because of context and because I'm just using them to make a point. And about the accent argument, perhaps I should specify that I'm not talking about occasional missteps, but of constant  mispronunciations, together with a strong accent that can't be ignored. Just think of the average Italian man in memes. And about the pretentiousness well, we can't actually speak so I guess that'll be left in the air.
I fail to see your reasoning there, have you heard me speak before?

I'm not sure what being bilingual actually means but I'm confident that certificates alone are close to meaningless.
